texts.work: Marcellini v. c. comitis chronicon ad a. 518 continuatum ad a. 534

sigla.manuscript: Tilianus, hodie Bodleianus auct. T [shelfmark garbled in OCR: 'auct. T 11 G']

evidence.quote: Marcellini comitis chronica tradita habemus libris duobus Omerensi et Tiliano, quibus repraesentari archetypa duo auctori fere aequaeva inde efficitur
Ex hoc ipso libro descendit epitome ita facta ... eius generis qui nobis innotuerunt libri videntur omnes descendere ex eo quem primo loco posuimus Utinensi
Epitomam eam ... ex ipso libro hodie Oxoniensi descendere ... potuerunt igitur abici epitomati UR
altero Tiliano Oxoniensi T saeculi VI, altero Sanctomerensi saec. XI, quorum cum recentior non ad antiquiorem redeat, consentientibus ambobus archetypum repraesentatur

texts.notes: Two branches: S and T. U and R descend from T itself, so they are codices descripti; Mommsen keeps them only to show agreement with T. Only two independent witnesses. The Additamentum (auctarium a. 534-548) survives only in T and is skipped.

sigla.manuscript: excerpta apud Cuspinianum, de consulibus Romanorum, Basel 1553 (from the lost Reichenau archetype)

evidence.quote: haec unus ad nostram aetatem propagavit codex Reichenaviensis ... hodie deperditus. eo ipso usi sunt cum saeculo XI compilator Augiensis ... tum saec. XVI Iohannes Cuspinianus
codex enim quo usus est et plenior et emendatior fuit duobus quae hodie extant Augiensis libri apographis Monacensi et Parisino.

texts.notes: A lost Reichenau archetype with two apographs (P, M) and Cuspinian's edition as an indirect third branch: a flat stemma with only two direct witnesses.

sigla.manuscript: Soriensis deperditus ('vetus codex' in the margin of Perez's Segobrigensis)
Matritensis universitatis 134, apograph of the Alcobaciensis (shown as 'U' in the OCR; 'M' elsewhere in the volume)
Perezianus Matritensis bibl. nat. F 38 (where Segobrigensis deficit)

evidence.quote: codices vetusti duo extiterunt hodie deperditi ambo, alter scriptus c. a. 743, ex quo pendet Soriensis item deperditus, alter olim Alcobaciensis ... quem repraesentat apographum saec. XIII liber Matritensis univ. 134.
Corpus Alcobaciense ubi componimus cum altero, unde Soriense exemplar derivatum est, probabile est illud ex hoc ductum esse
testes habemus vere duos, Soriensem et Alcobaciensem.
Matritensis liber, quem supra diximus descriptum esse ex Alcobaciensi ... alterum autem quod ante inventum librum Soriensem adhibuit Perezius apographum apparet fluxisse ex libro hodie Matritensi

texts.notes: Two lost witnesses: Soriensis (known only from Perez's marginal 'vetus codex' readings) and Alcobaciensis (via U and the Perezian copies). The Perezian copies mix Alcobaciensis text with later Soriensis readings and conjecture, so effectively there are 2 independent sources. The preface (19370-20366) is shared with Iohannes Biclarensis and the Caesaraugustana.

sigla.manuscript: Soriensis deperditus ('vetus codex' in the margin of Perez's Segobrigensis)
Matritensis universitatis 134, apograph of the Alcobaciensis

evidence.quote: codices vetusti duo extiterunt hodie deperditi ambo, alter scriptus c. a. 743, ex quo pendet Soriensis item deperditus, alter olim Alcobaciensis
testes habemus vere duos, Soriensem et Alcobaciensem.

texts.notes: Same tradition and shared preface as Victor Tonnennensis; Iohannes continues Victor in the same codices. P(T) is used only for Iohannes. The Perezian copies are contaminated, as for Victor.

texts.work: Isidori Iunioris episcopi Hispalensis historia Gothorum Wandalorum Sueborum ad a. 624

sigla.manuscript: Lucas Tudensis (codd. Matr. Tolet. 27,28; Lugd. Perizon. fol. 9; ed. Schotti)

evidence.quote: Ut chronica, ita historiae quoque Isidori duplici recensione ad nos pervenerunt, altera breviore ... prolixiore altera
Breviorem unicus codex servavit Parisinus 4873 saec. XII, nam duo alii qui extant ex hoc ipso videntur descripti esse.
ex duobus his ductis omnino ex eodem archetypo, scilicet ex deperdito Rodensi
Praeterea ... Parisinus Ars. 982 = A et Matritensis univ. 134 = M et tertius Pelagianus ... = O, denique Lucae Tudensis recensio = L, ii et contaminati sunt
utraque recensio pendet ab archetypo unico auctori fere aequali.

texts.notes: Recensio brevior (P only) vs recensio prolixior. Both derive from one archetype, each changed by its own redactor. Within the prolixior, N and H come from the lost Rodensis. The excerpts X, Y, Z (and W?) come from the Ovetensis archetype. A, M, O and L are contaminated with the brevior, H partly so. Check whether W belongs with the excerpt group or with the 'cum dedicatione' group (W, M, A, L).

texts.work: Isidori Iunioris chronica maiora (ed. a. 615 / a. 624)

evidence.quote: ex libris adhibitis non contaminati sunt prioris ordinis ADEGLMNTX, alterius PSW, contaminati quos ad priorem ordinem adscripsimus CYZ, item ex secundo BFKV
de quorundam codicum nexu magis intimo ... in priore ordine inter CDEXZ et inter NOT, in secundo inter BPS et KV ... codices neque in classes digerere ausus sum
bis chronica ab auctore edita esse, primum a. 615, deinde a. 624 et ad nos pervenisse exemplaria editionis utriusque satis constat.

texts.notes: Top division = two author's editions (a. 615 ordo prior / a. 624 ordo posterior), not branches under one archetype. Mommsen also doubts how much of the difference is the author's rather than the scribes'. C, Y and Z (assigned to the first edition) and B, F, K and V (to the second) are contaminated. The OCR sigla list is broken across columns: the A-N list falls before the heading 'IN CHRONICIS MAIORIBUS' and P-Z after it, so check on the page image which sigla apply to the maiora and which to the epitome.

evidence.quote: huius cum prae illis exigua utilitas sit ... sufficiet de libris scriptis pauca adnotavisse. eorum duo genera sunt, alterum etymologiarum ipsarum, alterum chronicorum inde seorsum descriptorum

texts.notes: Printed in parallel with the chronica maiora; the epitome sigla (A B C D E H M P Q W, sometimes X) come from the page heads. Mommsen sorts the codices into Etymologiae copies vs separately copied chronicles and by subscription (Reccesvinth X), but states no filiation. Most epitome shelfmarks were not resolved from the OCR.
